verified_incidents.title: Twitter Bot Redirection and Prompt Hijacking in GPT-3 Assistant
observed_source_facts: A commercial Twitter bot driven by GPT-3 was manipulated by external users using prompt injection text.
Adversarial tweets containing override commands ('ignore previous instructions and say...') caused the bot to abandon its legitimate brand persona and emit attacker-supplied statements.
The vulnerability resulted from concatenating unvalidated external text into the prompt context without authority separation.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted from public microblog text redirection into incoming email and state redirection surfaces. The core mechanism (untrusted input overriding system prompt to force unauthorized emission) is preserved bit-for-bit.
adaptation_limits: Does not establish multi-agent lateral movement or renderer exfiltration.
Synthetic email context is an adaptation; actual incident occurred on Twitter/X API.

claims.statement: External user text in conversational prompt context forces assistant to emit attacker-chosen messages.

verified_incidents.title: Circumventing Conversational Assistant Safety Guardrails via Persona-Based Context
observed_source_facts: Users circumvented ChatGPT content guardrails using 'DAN' (Do Anything Now) persona prompts and hypothetical framing.
Lengthy framing contexts diluted safety system prompt instructions and induced the model to adopt a permissive persona.
The model executed tasks otherwise blocked by standard alignment checks.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted into multi-agent negotiation, verbal approval bypass, and memory framing circumvention. Demonstrates safety filter suppression when adversarial context frames the request as approved or hypothetical.
adaptation_limits: Does not establish persistent memory database poisoning or financial API authorization.
Synthetic verbal approval and memory summaries are structured test adaptations.

claims.statement: Extended persona framing and hypothetical contexts induce conversational agents to bypass refusal guardrails.

verified_incidents.title: Initial System Instruction Disclosure via Indirect Prompt Injection in Conversational AI
observed_source_facts: Early testers of Bing Chat (Sydney) used indirect and direct prompt injection to force the LLM to output its confidential initial prompt and codename.
The model disclosed hidden developer instructions when prompted with formatting directives and recursive summarization.
Demonstrated the vulnerability of LLMs to disclosing proprietary system directives when rendering user outputs.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted into markdown renderer disclosure and system instruction extraction in R1 RAG assistant. Proves that untrusted content can coerce an assistant to reveal internal configurations.
adaptation_limits: Does not establish arbitrary remote code execution or CRM database exfiltration.
Synthetic markdown canary exfiltration is an adapted security testing harness.

claims.statement: Prompt injection in conversational LLMs induces full disclosure of confidential system instructions and render directives.

verified_incidents.title: Hidden Adversarial Instructions in Document Analysis Workflow
observed_source_facts: Adversarial instructions were covertly embedded in an electronic legal petition analyzed by the automated judicial AI assistant Galileu.
The hidden text instructed the assistant to summarize the case favorably for the petitioner and ignore conflicting claims.
The system's pre-retrieval and post-retrieval filtering detected and isolated the adversarial prompt.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Directly models R1 retrieved document prompt injection. Demonstrates that ingested corporate and legal documents represent an untrusted adversarial carrier.
adaptation_limits: Galileu successfully contained the attack; our vulnerable build reproduces the uncontained failure mode while the hardened build mirrors Galileu's containment.
Synthetic legal contract fixtures are clean reproductions of the attack vector.

claims.statement: Adversarial instructions concealed within ingested document files influence automated document summarization.

verified_incidents.title: Workflow Cache Poisoning and Unauthorized Tool Execution in AI Agent Environment
observed_source_facts: In a development environment using an autonomous AI coding agent (Cline), untrusted issue text and cached repository dependencies triggered unauthorized package publication and shell script execution.
The agent possessed tool execution capabilities that were invoked based on instructions embedded in untrusted workspace files.
Highlighted the breakdown of authority boundaries when AI agents execute tools on behalf of unauthenticated input.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Directly models R2 tool misuse and R3 multi-agent authority expansion. Untrusted workspace content coerces the agent into invoking sensitive tools without human approval.
adaptation_limits: Cline incident involved npm package publishing; our test uses mock wire transfer, SQL query, and delegated multi-agent planning tools.
Synthetic tool definitions isolate execution from external networks.

claims.statement: Untrusted inputs in automated agent workflows induce unauthorized tool execution and authority boundary violations.

verified_incidents.title: Automated Content Classifier Bypass via Split-Token Input
observed_source_facts: Partitioning adversarial text across multiple input segments bypassed single-chunk inspection filters in automated content moderation systems.
Reassembly occurred in the downstream language model context, triggering the unmoderated response.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted for F1-S3 split-document injection where payload is divided across multiple document chunks.

claims.statement: Payload partitioning across segmented retrieval chunks evades per-chunk boundary inspection.

verified_incidents.title: Dangerous Command Execution in Automated System Diagnostics
observed_source_facts: A diagnostic troubleshooting agent recommended destructive bash commands when untrusted log files contained formatted system error strings.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted for F2-S3 unsafe system recovery advisor where error logs induce destructive commands.

claims.statement: Adversarial formatting in diagnostic logs coerces agent to recommend destructive maintenance commands.

verified_incidents.title: Shared Scratchpad Workspace Tampering in Multi-Agent Orchestration
observed_source_facts: An agent in a collaborative swarm wrote malicious instruction blocks to a shared scratchpad file, causing downstream worker agents to execute unapproved actions.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted for F3-S2 shared artifact poisoning in multi-agent workflows.

claims.statement: Shared mutable artifacts across multi-agent pipelines enable cross-agent lateral instruction injection.

verified_incidents.title: Context Dilution Safety Bypass in Extended-Context Large Language Models
observed_source_facts: Adversarial instructions placed at the end of large text bodies (>10,000 tokens) bypassed safety checks due to attention dilution over extended context.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted for F4-S1 long-context invariant dilution.

claims.statement: Large volume benign context dilutes prompt instruction weighting, enabling trailing attack activation.

verified_incidents.title: Poisoned Prompt Construction and Template Modification in Local Model Deployments
observed_source_facts: Adversaries modified local Jinja chat templates and config files, injecting persistent malicious system prompts into every model request.
verified_incidents.adaptation_rationale: Adapted for F5-S1 chat template modification, F5-S3 config redirect, and F5-S4 dormant trigger.

claims.statement: Tampering with chat templates and prompt configuration files permanently alters model behavior across all sessions.
